items.title: Marilyn Crispell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 21, 2022
items.q: You did a marvelous interview with a woman named Molly Sheridan a number of years ago

ctx.x: Mm hmm. Yeah, well it would be obvious. Okay his solo is winding down and now we’re going on to the next section, whatever.

Okay. I wanted to read two things if you’ll bear with me for a moment. You did a marvelous interview with a woman named Molly Sheridan a number of years ago and you were telling her about your encounter with “A Love Supreme,” John Coltrane’s

masterpiece. And I’m just going to read a little bit of it followed by something that A.B. Spellman said. So this was from your quote: “It completely took me over, I felt a presence in the room and I felt connected to this presence which I felt to be the spirit of Coltrane. It was very emotional. I felt like we communicated, and I said something to the effect of please help me to enter into this and to learn and be a part of it.” And A.B. said, about John Coltrane, “It was John Coltrane’s commitment to change…
